title: Advancements in Pipeline Corrosion Monitoring for Supercritical CO2 Environments: A Review
source: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
summary: A review of corrosion evaluation and monitoring techniques for pipelines carrying CO2 in the supercritical state. The authors note that impurities such as water, SO2, O2, H2S and NO2 make supercritical-CO2 corrosion a major challenge for pipeline transport, and that earlier reviews focused on mechanisms and prevention rather than monitoring.
why_it_matters: Impurity limits and corrosion monitoring requirements shape CO2 stream specifications, pipeline material choices and operating costs in shared multi-emitter pipeline networks.
authors: Prosper Dadzie, Aliyu Adebayo Sulaimon, Shiferaw Regassa Jufar, Yen Adams Sokama‐Neuyam, Joshua Nsiah Turkson, Muhammad Ayoub et al.
approved_by: Published automatically (before the review step existed)
